newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Banco Sotto's star not waning.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Banco Sotto's star not waning.

text.p: Portugal's Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor (BPSM), whose share price has more than doubled in a two month surge, could rise further because investor enthusiasm shows no sign of waning, analysts said on Friday.
The Champalimaud group bank has eclipsed sister bank Banco Totta & Acores which was once favoured because it had the reputation of being one of the best dividend payers on the Portuguese market.
Banco Sotto, which announced a 194 percent rise in first half profit on Thursday to 8.4 billion escudos ($45 million), gained a further eight percent to 2,298 escudos on Friday.
The sharp profit rise had been widely predicted and was one of the factors propelling the stock upwards in recent sessions.
Some analyst said that the share could target 3,000 escudos providing there were no negative announcements over the second half of the year, such as increased provisions for pension funds.

"Sotto could outpace the (overall) bourse. If it goes on at this rate, it could reach 3,000 escudos by the end of the year but everything depends on group policy over the second half of the year," said one analyst who refused to be named.
He said the gains could be accompanied by Mundial Confianca, the insurance company which acts as financial holding for the Champalimaud group and its banks.

"The group made no extraordinary provisions for pensions, but if they decide to do so in the second half, in order to get tax benefits, this could have a negative impact on profit and the share price," the analyst added.
Analysts said that there had clearly been some investor switching out of Banco Totta into Banco Sotto.
"Banco Sotto has become more and more the star of the group. The performance over the first half was very good and the full-year profit is also going to be very favourable," said another analyst.
Some analysts were already beginning to revise upwards their expectations for Banco Sotto's 1997 profit, with the first analyst saying he was raising his by 50 percent to some 18.3 billion escudos.

Despite the sharp rise, which has seen the share jump from 1,113 escudos in late May, analysts said that it was still trading at a discount to some other Portuguese banks such as Banco Espirito Santo and Banco Comercial Portugues .
They added that Banco Sotto also appeared to be taking an increasing role in the emerging restructuring of the Champalimaud group's financial holdings.
In contrast, analysts said that Banco Totta's first half figures pointed to low growth in its banking activities in the second quarter.
"I cannot think of any reason why, in a quarter which was highly dynamic for the sector as a whole, Totta presented such a low figure for banking turnover.
"It is clear that the Banco Sotto is taking the lead (in the group)," said another analyst.
